title: stabilization-window-rc-eligibility-orchestrator
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current weekly build -> RC tagging flow relies on ad-hoc human checks and a separate release notes generation step. This causes two recurring issues: 1) borderline builds get promoted without a predictable stability gate, increasing hotfix churn on LTS lanes; 2) release notes are assembled manually from PR templates and often miss runtime-impacting changes (batching, KV cache, kernel selection) unless authors explicitly tag them.

Goal: Implement a stabilization-window + RC eligibility orchestrator that programmatically evaluates candidate weekly builds across signal tiers (test flakes, canary SLO deltas, perf regressions, eval quality checks) and produces: (a) an explicit RC candidate list with provenance and confidence score; (b) automated RC tagging in git for eligible candidates; (c) automated release notes draft enriched with runtime-impact metadata and links to performance dashboards. The orchestrator should also expose a small human review UI in Console to approve/override candidates before final tagging for the weekly LTS lane.

High level proposal:
- Stabilization window: run a deterministic 48-hour window after each weekly build where the orchestrator aggregates signals and computes an "eligibility_score" per build. Signals include flaky test score (30%), canary SLO delta (30%), per-token latency regression (20%), eval-suite regression rate (15%), and security policy scans (5%).
- RC eligibility rules engine: translate score + hard gates into an outcome: eligible/conditional/blocked. Hard gates: critical test failures, policy scan failures, or >2% canary SLO regression => blocked. Conditional builds require human review.
- RC tagging automation: for eligible builds, create a lightweight release branch and annotate with metadata (build id, score, signal links), then tag git as rc-{semver}-{date}. If conditional, mark in Console and create a reviewer assignment.
- Release notes automation: use PR metadata, label heuristics, and runtime changelog parsers (scan commit messages for keys like BATCHING, KV_CACHE, KERNEL) to synthesize a structured notes draft. Enrich with links to: perf dashboard (grafana), integration test run (CI URL), and eval diff (s3 path). Also include a human-editable summary in Console.

Non-goals: full replacement of human judgment for exceptional releases; automatic LTS promotion without explicit approval.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict numeric gating vs. fuzzy scoring: chosen hybrid (score + hard gates) to balance automation with engineer oversight.
- Time window length: 48h is a compromise between fast weekly cadence and collecting meaningful stability signals. Can be tuned via config.
- Complexity of release-note NLP: initial implementation will be rule-based heuristics to keep scope small; later iterations may add ML-based grouping.

Operational notes:
- The orchestrator will run as a daily job in the release namespace and listen for new weekly build events.
- All decisions are recorded in a release provenance log with links to artifacts for audit.
- Console feature flags will gate auto-tagging and the human-review UI so we can do staged rollout to internal teams first.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator aggregates signals and computes eligibility score for a weekly build within 1 hour of window close
Eligible builds are auto-tagged with RC tags in main git repository when auto-tagging feature flag is enabled
Conditional builds surface in Console with reviewer assignment and a concise provenance panel
Release notes draft is generated for every candidate and includes links to perf dashboard, CI run, and eval diff
All decisions are logged and queryable via the release provenance dashboard
